channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Eyes further upside towards 1.1620
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades subduedly at around 1.1550 against the US Dollar (USD) during the early European trading session on Monday. The EUR/USD pair edges down as the US Dollar rebounds after a significant fall on Friday.

item.title: Indian Rupee drops as oil prices extend recovery, downside seems limited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens on a negative note against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week. The USD/INR pair rebounds to near 95.22 as oil prices extend their recovery move and the US Dollar regains ground after a weak Friday.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bulls await sustained move above $78.00 amid supply concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – kicks off the new week on a positive note amid the US-Iran standoff over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah struggles as Consumer Confidence drops to weakest level since September 2025
item.description: USD/IDR holds gains after registering over 0.5% losses in the previous trading day, hovering around 17,860 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair continues to trade with an upward bias as the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) faces pressure following the release of domestic Consumer Confidence data.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Gold remains on the back foot below June 17 high amid USD uptick; downside seems cushioned
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) drifts lower at the start of a new week and moves away from its highest level since June 17, touched on Friday following the disappointing release of the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: Swiss Franc declines as safe-haven demand supports US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF inches higher after registering over 0.5% losses in the previous trading day, hovering around 0.8090 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar drifts lower as USD recovers from post-NFP lows amid Mideast jitters
item.description: The NZD/USD pair is seen extending Friday's late pullback from the vicinity of the monthly peak – levels just above the 0.5900 mark – and drifting lower at the start of a new week.

item.title: United States Dollar Index advances above 99.50 due to Middle East risks
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is gaining ground after registering modest losses in the previous day and trading around 99.70 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD starts US CPI week on flat note around $63.50
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades in a tight range at around $63.50 during the Asian trading session at the start of the week. The white metal struggles for direction but is close to an almost seven-week high of $65.16 posted on Friday.

item.title: Australian Dollar weakens as safe-haven demand lifts US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD inches lower after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around 0.7060 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair holds losses as the US Dollar (USD) receives support from broad risk aversion.

item.title: Canadian Dollar pulls back from two-month top as rebounding USD counters higher oil prices
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts some dip-buyers at the start of a new week and recovers a part of Friday's heavy losses to the 1.3925 area, or a nearly two-month low.

item.title: Japanese Yen comes under pressure as BoJ division, unexpected current account deficit
item.description: USD/JPY gains ground after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 158.20 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: British Pound moves away from multi-week top as Hormuz risks support USD
item.description: The GBP/USD pair edges lower at the start of a new week and moves further away from an over three-week high, or levels just above the 1.3500 psychological mark touched on Friday.

item.title: Euro consolidates below its highest level since June 17 as Mideast tensions support USD
item.description: The EUR/USD pair kicks off the new week on a subdued note and trades just above 1.1550 during the Asian session, well within striking distance of a fresh high since June 17, touched in reaction to the disappointing US jobs data on Friday.

item.title: Hormuz tensions escalate as unconfirmed missile attack amid fragile US-Iran talks
item.description: The ongoing US-Iran conflict has entered a crucial diplomatic phase, with intense fighting and strategic pressure around the vital Strait of Hormuz continuing to drive the dynamic of the war.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7884 vs. 6.7904 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7884 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7904 and 6.7379 Reuters estimate.

item.title: BoJ Summary of Opinions: Board split on pace of rate hikes amid inflation risk
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) published the Summary of Opinions from the July 30-31 monetary policy meeting, which showed a split between members wanting to hold rates to assess the impact of the last rate hike and others pushing to continue or accelerate tightening. Key findings noted below.

item.title: WTI rises to near $79.50 amid uncertainty over reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price gains ground after registering nearly 1.5% losses in the previous trading day, hovering around $79.40 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday. Crude oil prices advance as persistent uncertainty surrounds efforts to reopen the critical Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: China: Credit demand and liquidity trends – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research anticipates China’s credit demand to stay weak in July, with new Yuan loans around RMB 10.8 billion and M2 growth at 8% year-on-year. Corporate and household medium- to long-term lending are likely to soften amid cautious borrowing and mortgage prepayments.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade holds with bullish tone against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see USD/CNH confined to a narrow intraday range, with flat momentum suggesting consolidation between 6.7450 and 6.7550.

item.title: Singapore: GDP revision and forecast upgrade – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research expects Singapore’s final 2Q26 GDP to be revised up to 5.9% year-on-year and 1.3% quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted, driven by stronger manufacturing and services.

item.title: Hormuz deal hopes rise as talks progress – Reuters
item.description: A US official said on Friday that there is progress in Oman-Iran talks and that a deal could be signed soon, according to Reuters. Once the deal is announced, this would restore commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and the US would lift the blockade.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Rebound holds above 200-day SMA
item.description: The British Pound retreats against the Japanese Yen, down about 0.24%, as the Yen is poised to end the week on a higher note. However, GBP/JPY is poised to finish the week with minimal gains, trading at 212.64.

item.title: Philippines: BSP policy outlook shifts – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Jonathan Koh and Edward Lee now expect Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to keep its policy rate unchanged at the 27 August meeting, abandoning a previously projected hike.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US inflation takes center stage next week
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell below the 100.00 region after sinking through Friday's session. July Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) showed the US economy shedding 23K jobs against forecasts of an 80K gain, with June revised down to 20K, and Average Hourly Earnings slowing to 3.2% on the year.

item.title: US Treasury yields drop on soft NFP, Hormuz hopes ease Fed risks
item.description: US Treasury yields drop across the curve on Friday amid growing speculation that the Iran-Oman deal is about to be sealed, which has so far pushed energy prices lower, while investors also digest a weak Nonfarm Payrolls report in the US.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Supportive domestic backdrop, capped gains – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX analysts, including Charlie Lay and Moses Lim, note that USD/IDR slipped slightly but stayed below the key 18,000 level as softer global Oil prices and stronger Indonesia Q2 GDP supported the Rupiah.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD clears 50-day SMA, eyes $65
item.description: Silver price surges nearly 3% as it clears the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $62.13, and reclaims the $63.00 figure as it struggles to surpass key resistance seen at $63.28, the July 6 high.

item.title: EUR/JPY recovers from session low but remains down on Friday
item.description: EUR/JPY trades on the back foot on Friday, easing away even as the Euro (EUR) posts solid gains against the US Dollar (USD). The Japanese currency surged suddenly near the start of the American session after a surprisingly weak United States (US) employment report.
